kjv: wherefore do ye tempt the LORD?
note: nissah means to test or put to the proof. Today "tempt" means to entice to sin. Same in v. 7.
wayyachalosh means he defeated or disabled them. "Discomfited" now means made uneasy.

kjv: Because the LORD hath sworn that the LORD will have war
mine: A hand upon the throne of Yah!
note: yad 'al-kes yah is obscure: "kes" is not a known word; it is read as a short form of kisse' "throne" (the KJV, following the Targum, takes "hand upon the throne" as an oath) or as nes "banner". Context decides for "banner": v.15 names the altar Yahweh-nissi, "Yahweh is my banner", and Moses' raised hands (17:11-12) are the rallying sign of the battle. Context: A hand upon the throne of Yah (medium confidence). MT kes is most simply a short form of kisse' 'throne'; the Samaritan Pentateuch reads ks', and the Vulgate (solii) and Targums read 'throne'. 'Banner' requires emending kes to nes, attractive after v.15 (Yahweh-nissi) but unsupported by any witness. ESV, NIV, NJPS, CSB and NET read 'throne'. Whose hand, raised in oath or against the throne, is left open. Other possible meanings: (1) 'a hand upon the banner of Yah' (emending to nes, cf. 17:15) — NRSV, many critical commentators; (2) an oath, 'Yahweh has sworn' (hand raised upon the throne) — Targum, Rashi, KJV, NASB95; (3) Amalek's hand raised against Yahweh's throne — NIV; (4) 'with a hidden hand' (from ksh 'cover') — LXX.
